text:
Recent work supports separating persistent preferences from recent intent, though it does not establish gains on this exact benchmark. [MSMT-LSI (2024)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44196-024-00460-5) combines temporal embeddings with separate long-/short-term attention networks; it reports improvements on sparse Amazon Beauty/Games, while acknowledging weaker performance with limited histories. [HeteroTempRec (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0020025525008369) combines local convolutions, global Transformer dependencies, temporal adaptive fusion, and gated historical blocks. These provide architectural precedents for learning when recent behavior should outweigh older interests.

Multi-interest modeling offers another direction. [D2MFRec (2025)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-31190-z) gates single-interest and multiple-interest representations, then applies denoising contrastive learning; its discussion flags overly dispersed dynamic-routing representations under sparse, irregular behavior. [MIMAR-SRec (2026)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38489) models intent across contextual windows with prototype alignment and robustness training. Practical inference for a lightweight SASRec trial: retain its recent-context representation, add masked historical pooling with a few learned interest queries, and learn a sigmoid fusion gate conditioned on representations, observed history length, and timestamp gaps. Ablate pooling, gating, and multiple interests separately against tuned SASRec. These papers motivate the hypothesis; they do not validate improvement under the specified four-category, sampled-candidate macro HR@10 protocol.
